qs.q: Position A 45° N, ?° E; position B 45° N, 45° 15'E. Distance A–B = 350 NM, B is to the east of A. What is the longitude of position A?
qs.ex: Δlong = distance / cos lat = 350 / cos 45° ≈ 495' = 8° 15'. A is west of B: 45° 15' − 8° 15' = 37° 00' E.

qs.q: The 'departure' between position 60°N 100°E and 60° N 'X' is 1200 NM. What is the longitude of 'X'?
qs.ex: Δlong = departure / cos lat = 1200 / 0.5 = 2400' = 40°, so 100° E + 40° = 140° E.

qs.q: Two aircraft are flying eastwards around the earth. Aircraft A is flying along the 50N parallel of latitude and aircraft B along the equator. If aircraft A is flying at a groundspeed of 340 knots, what would be the groundspeed of aircraft B if both aircraft fly once round the Earth in the same journey time?
qs.ex: Equal journey time means GS is in proportion to the length of the parallel: 340 / cos 50° ≈ 529 kt.

qs.ex: ATIS winds are magnetic. Angle between wind 210° and runway 047° = 163°, so tailwind = V × cos 17° ≈ 0.956 V. 10 / 0.956 ≈ 10.5 → about 11 kt.

qs.q: Course required = 085° (T), Forecast W/V 030/100kt, TAS = 470 kt, Distance = 265nm. Calculate the true HDG and flight time?
